name: chocolate cake
instructions:
From Sally McKenney (Sally's Baking Recipes), 'Triple Chocolate Cake' — cake portion only, skipping the chocolate buttercream. Two 9-inch round layers OR one 9x13 sheet. Extra moist, fudgy but light. Adapted from Ina Garten / originally Hershey's.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 3/4 cups (219g) all-purpose flour (spooned & leveled — NOT cake flour, see notes)
- 3/4 cup (64g) unsweetened NATURAL cocoa powder (NOT dutch-process — see notes)
- 1 3/4 cups (350g) granulated sugar
- 2 tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 tsp espresso powder (optional but recommended — see notes)
- 1/2 cup (120ml) vegetable oil (or canola or melted coconut oil — NOT butter, see notes)
- 2 large eggs, at room temperature
- 2 tsp pure vanilla extract
- 1 cup (240ml) buttermilk, at room temperature (required — see DIY sub in notes)
- 1 cup (240ml) freshly brewed strong HOT coffee or hot water (see notes)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C). Grease two 9-inch cake pans, line with parchment paper rounds, then grease the parchment paper. (Or use a 9x13-inch pan for a sheet cake — see notes.)
2. WHISK DRY INGREDIENTS: in a large bowl, whisk together the flour, natural cocoa powder, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and espresso powder (if using). Set aside.
3. WHISK WET INGREDIENTS: using a handheld or stand mixer with whisk attachment (or just a whisk), mix the oil, eggs, and vanilla until combined. Add the buttermilk and mix until combined.
4. COMBINE + ADD HOT LIQUID: pour the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients, add the hot coffee/water, and whisk or beat on low speed until the batter is completely combined. Batter will be thin — that's correct.
5. Divide the batter evenly between the prepared pans.
6. BAKE: 23-26 min at 350°F, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Even when done, the cooled cakes may slightly sink in the center — that's normal for a cocoa-heavy cake.
7. COOL: cool the cakes in the pans set on a cooling rack for 1 hour. Run a knife around the edges to loosen, remove from pans, peel off parchment, place on the cooling rack to finish cooling.

SHEET CAKE VERSION: bake in a 9x13-inch pan at the same 350°F for ~35-40 min.

3-LAYER VERSION: divide the batter between three 8-inch cake pans; bake for 22-25 min.
notes:
Source: Sally McKenney (Sally's Baking Recipes), 'Triple Chocolate Cake.' Adapted from Ina Garten / originally Hershey's. Frosting (chocolate buttercream) intentionally skipped in this cookbook entry — the cake is the load-bearing part; pair with whatever frosting fits the occasion.

=== NATURAL COCOA POWDER — NOT DUTCH-PROCESS ===

MUST BE NATURAL, NOT DUTCH-PROCESS: this recipe specifically calls for unsweetened NATURAL cocoa powder. Dutch-process cocoa is treated with an alkalizing agent that neutralizes the natural acidity of cocoa; without that acidity, the baking soda in this recipe doesn't have anything to react with, and the leavening fails. Sally's note is explicit: save the dutch-process for other recipes.

This cookbook now has two distinct cocoa ingredients:
- NATURAL cocoa powder — acidic, fruity, more assertive chocolate flavor. Used in mexican cooking and in recipes with baking soda as the leavener. THIS RECIPE.
- DUTCH PROCESS cocoa powder — alkalized, smoother, less acidic. Used in recipes where the acid isn't needed for leavening (e.g., recipes leavened by baking powder or eggs alone).
They're not interchangeable in leavened baking. Match the cocoa to what the recipe's leavening chemistry expects.

=== ALL-PURPOSE FLOUR, NOT CAKE FLOUR ===

Sally is explicit: don't use cake flour. Cake flour combined with the ultra-light natural cocoa powder is too fine for this cake — no structure. All-purpose is what the recipe is engineered around.

=== VEGETABLE OIL, NOT BUTTER ===

Cocoa powder is a drying ingredient. Oil (vegetable, canola, or melted coconut) provides more consistent moisture through the bake than butter would. Same reason Sally's chocolate cake roll uses oil. Don't sub butter here.

=== BUTTERMILK IS REQUIRED — DIY IF NEEDED ===

The recipe needs both the moisture AND the acidity of buttermilk (acid reinforces the natural cocoa's reaction with the baking soda). DIY sub: 2 tsp white vinegar or lemon juice + enough room-temp whole milk to make 1 cup total. Stir, let sit 5 min. Somewhat curdled = ready.

=== HOT COFFEE (OR HOT WATER) — LOAD-BEARING ===

Hot liquid enhances the cocoa flavor and helps bloom / dissolve the cocoa powder. This isn't optional in the sense of skipping the hot-liquid step — you need the volume and the temperature. Coffee (regular or decaf) gives deeper, darker flavor than water; the cake will NOT taste like coffee. If coffee isn't your thing, use hot water.

=== ESPRESSO POWDER — OPTIONAL BUT RECOMMENDED ===

Enhances the chocolate flavor. Cake won't taste like coffee. Find it in the coffee or baking aisle. Instant coffee powder is a valid substitute (same amount).

=== ROOM-TEMPERATURE INGREDIENTS ===

All refrigerated items (eggs, buttermilk) should be at room temperature so the batter mixes evenly. Cold eggs: place in warm water for 10 min.

=== TWO CAKE VARIATIONS SALLY DESCRIBES ===

- ORIGINAL VERSION (this recipe): very thin batter. Extra soft, deliciously spongey texture.
- SOUR CREAM VERSION (Sally's alternate): reduce buttermilk and hot coffee to 1/2 cup each; add 3/4 cup (180g) full-fat sour cream with the wet ingredients. Slightly thicker batter, slightly denser cake with more structure. Both are equally moist and chocolatey; pick based on whether you want spongier or sturdier.

=== FROSTING NOTES (SKIPPED IN THIS ENTRY) ===

Sally pairs this with chocolate buttercream (butter + confectioners sugar + cocoa + heavy cream + vanilla + salt). Not captured here. Any frosting that pairs with chocolate cake — chocolate buttercream, vanilla buttercream, peanut butter frosting, cream cheese frosting — is a valid pairing. NOTE: in a frosting (no leavening involved), either natural or dutch-process cocoa works, since the leavening-chemistry constraint doesn't apply.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- french-yogurt-cake: lemon-forward yogurt-based cake. Tried a chocolate variant of it (AUG 13 2026 experiment there) and it didn't turn out — spongey/flat and fruity/funky. The french-yogurt-cake base is tuned for lemon and doesn't retool cleanly to chocolate. This recipe (Sally's) is the actual chocolate cake path — built from the ground up for chocolate, with the right leavening chemistry for natural cocoa.
- panna-cotta: chocolate variant uses natural cocoa powder (double-boiler method).
